ut_inception.blurb: Inception is a compact cluster of 15 boulder problems beside the road in Little Cottonwood Canyon, just below Snowbird resort at roughly 7,900 feet. The elevation keeps it cooler than the lower canyon, and the setting is a grove of aspens, which makes it a pleasant summer stop. The grades lean hard: about half the problems sit between V4 and V8, while the other half are V10 or V11, so this is a stop for strong boulderers rather than a beginner circuit. A short trail leads to the blocks from the roadside, and the hardest lines here are well known across the canyon.

ut_eastern_boulder.blurb: Eastern Boulder is a small bouldering stop in the Warm-up Area of White Pine South, one of the White Pine boulder groups in Little Cottonwood Canyon. It holds about 15 problems and is friendly overall: nearly all fall between V0 and V4, with the largest share at V3 or easier, plus one far harder problem near V8. That spread makes it a good place to loosen up before moving to bigger blocks, and a reasonable pick for newer boulderers who want a handful of well-liked easy and moderate problems close together.

ut_unemployment_wall.blurb: Unemployment Wall is the first cliff you reach on the trail at Pine Valley, a basalt venue near St. George. It holds 15 routes: nine sport and six trad. Grades cluster in the 5.11 range, with a few 5.9 and 5.10 lines and a single 5.12. The climbing is technical face work on basalt, with ledges on the cliff that make a helmet sensible, and routes run up to about 100 feet. Shade moves across the wall from early to mid afternoon, so the later hours are the comfortable ones on warm days. Unchalked routes can be hard to read.

ut_asbury_park_2.blurb: Asbury Park is one of the northern walls of the Schoolroom, a long band of tiered quartzite cliffs on the east side of Ogden. It is the hard-routes wall of the Schoolroom: 15 climbs, nine sport and six trad, with most between 5.10 and 5.13 and only a pair of easier trad lines. Unclimbed projects remain on the wall. Lower and side tiers nearby, including The Basement and Gangsta' Ledge, add more routes. The walk up is fairly long and steep, following a grassy ramp, and the area stays quieter than the more popular Ogden crags.

ut_mullein_land.blurb: Mullein Land is a crag in Logan Canyon, at about 5,400 feet, with 15 climbs: eleven sport and four trad. Grades start at an easy 5.5 and reach 5.12, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.11, so it works for a mixed-ability group. It sees fewer climbers than some neighbouring walls, which keeps the rock in good condition. Most lines are exposed, so wind and sun can matter on some days, and a couple of routes call for a 70 m rope or a two-rope rappel. The walk in is short, about 0.2 mile, but climbs a fair amount of elevation on a steepish trail.
ut_mullein_land.approach: A short trail begins across the road from the roadside pullout, about 0.2 mile and a couple of hundred feet of uphill; it runs just west of the rocks and turns steep in places.

ut_brighton_s_frighton_wall.blurb: Brighton's Frighton Wall is a small crag in the Brighton area of Big Cottonwood Canyon, around 9,000 feet. It has 15 routes, mostly trad (eleven) with four sport lines, ranging from about 5.8 to 5.12 with the majority at 5.9 and 5.10. The high elevation keeps temperatures cool and the spot feels secluded. Climbers praise the quality of the rock, and the main drawback is that the routes are short. It suits a relaxed day of moderate crack and face climbing in the Wasatch alpine.

ut_vertical_smile_wall.blurb: Vertical Smile Wall is a buttress beside the road in Lower Buckhorn, within Buckhorn Wash in the San Rafael Swell. It holds about 15 climbs, mostly trad (twelve), with a pair of aid lines and a single sport route. The free climbing runs from 5.7 up to 5.11, with the most routes at 5.9 and 5.10, and the hardest lines are the best known here. The wall is on the east side of the road, just north of a neighbouring wall, so the walk from the car is minimal. It offers a mix of moderate and difficult desert trad in one spot.
